chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:

translations.en: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, that he said:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلٍ تَصَدَّقَ عَلَى وُلْدٍ لَهُ قَدْ أَدْرَكُوا فَقَالَ: «إِذَا لَمْ يَقْبِضُوا حَتَّى يَمُوتَ فَهِيَ مِيرَاثٌ فَإِنْ تَصَدَّقَ عَلَى مَنْ لَمْ يُدْرِكْ مِنْ وُلْدِهِ فَهُوَ جَائِزٌ لِأَنَّ الْوَالِدَ هُوَ الَّذِي يَلِي أَمْرَهُمْ»

translations.en: Regarding a man who gave charity to children of his who had reached maturity, he said: "If they do not take possession before he dies, then it is inheritance. But if he gives charity to those among his children who have not reached maturity, then it is valid, because the father is the one who administers their affairs."

chunks.arabic_text: وَ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: «لَا يَرْجِعْ فِي الصَّدَقَةِ إِذَا تَصَدَّقَ بِهَا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ».

translations.en: And he عليه السلام said: "He should not take back the charity when he has given it seeking the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

en.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling about charity given by a father to his children. If adult children do not take possession before the father's death, the property returns to the estate as inheritance, whereas charity to minor children is valid because the father oversees their affairs. It also teaches that charity given sincerely for Allah should not be taken back.
en.seo_question: When does charity given to one's children become inheritance, and can it be taken back?

key_terms.الْوَالِدَ: the father who administers the child’s affairs
